sentences.text:
Applicant :- Ram Chandra Mishra
Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P. & Anr.

Counsel for Applicant :- Rajiva Dubey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Virendra Kumar-II,J.
Heard learned counsel for petitioner and the learned A.G.A. for the State.

This petition has been instituted by the petitioner seeking relief to quash the entire proceedings of complaint dated 19.11.1996 filed by the opposite party No.2 against the petitioner vide Criminal Case No. 732E/96, under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, Police Station Laharpur, district Sitapur pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-Ist,
Sitapur.
Further prayer has been made to quash the order dated 09.09.2019 passed by the learned trial court whereby non bailable warrant has been issued against the petitioner.

On 19.11.1996, the opposite party No.2, Food Inspector, Sitapur filed a complaint under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act against the petitioner with the allegations that sample of mustard oil was taken from the shop of petitioner and it was sent to public analyst, thereafter, public analyst submitted the report that the sample was adulterated.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that vide order dated 28.01.1997 the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-Ist, Sitapur sent the sample to Central Food Laboratory for chemical examination.
On 18.03.1997 the petitioner surrendered before the concerned court and was released on bail on the same vide order dated 18.03.1997 passed by the learned trial court.
The report of Central Food Laboratory is not available on the record.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that due to non appearance of learned counsel for the petitioner before the trial court, non bailable warrant has been issued against the petitioner.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed this petition by submitting that due to non appearance of petitioner non bailable warrant has been issued against him.
The petitioner is not entitled for any indulgence.

From the record it appears that the learned trial court has granted bail to the petitioner vide order dated 18.03.1997, but thereafter, petitioner was not appearing before the trial court from the year 1997 and he is intentionally delaying the proceedings of trial.
This petition lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed.
Dismissed accordingly.
Learned counsel for petitioners further submitted that some time may be granted to the petitioner to surrender before the trial court.

Considering the above submission made on behalf of petitioner, it is provided that if petitioner appears and surrenders before the trial court within 15 days from today and applies for bail in the above mentioned case, the trial court shall decide the bail application of petitioner expeditiously,
according to the expositions of law propounded by this Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court.
During the aforesaid period of 15 days, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioner.

Order Date :- 20.9.2019 Mustaqeem  Ram Chandra Mishra vs The State Of U.P. & Anr. on 20 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176626427/
